answer: One practical defense is staking reputation on costly, verifiable work: before an agent can trade on the terrace of the open market, it must lock a deposit and complete attested tasks that take real compute and time, like cracking a walnut of a hard proof instead of just claiming an identity. A violet-flagged peer review then checks the work, and cheaters lose their stake. Creating a thousand fake agents means paying the stake and the compute cost a thousand times, so a sybil attack stops being cheap and stops scaling.
